analysis: Reviewed the two base_text units of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (base lines 21630-23288). These contain only public synthetic test vectors: repeated 'Public followup.' and 'Public synthetic cache-parity input.' text, token_ids, prompt_contract_id, block_boundaries and chain hashes. No secrets, credentials, keys, or consumer data appear. The patch excerpt (truncated, but range map complete) changes template_input by adding additional_context {enable_thinking:false}, prompt_token_count and chain_hash values, and removes a block boundary. These are golden-vector fixture updates, with no executable code, authorization, attestation or encryption logic changed in this file. The relevant threat context is the T-041 prefix-cache and prompt-contract area. The chain hashes and token IDs are test oracles that must stay consistent with the Swift provider's prompt-rendering and plan code, and with the coordinator's. Whether the new vectors match the actual implementation changes (for example enable_thinking handling) lives in other files outside this batch. A mismatch there would produce only a parity-test failure or cache-key divergence, and no vulnerability is evidenced here. Several changed head ranges (e.g. around head lines 43739, 44524, 52354) were not visible in the supplied base units, so they were not examined directly. The next pass should confirm that the source changes behind the new additional_context rendering do not alter cache-key isolation or the tenant scoping of prefix-cache chain hashes. The scope_id 'fixture-scope' is a synthetic value.
